figures.finding: Antarctica has no government of its own: the Antarctic Treaty freezes territorial claims and leaves treaty personnel under their own country's jurisdiction, so a person working there takes their home country's tax; Australia counts its Antarctic Territory inside its income tax (Zone A), and the British Antarctic Territory levies its own 7% income tax, but only on British Antarctic Survey staff employed in the Territory for a continuous 365 days; France taxes its own nationals working in Terre Adélie through the TAAF's 9% contribution directe territoriale; a visiting foreign film crew owes no Antarctic tax under any of these.

value.rule: the worker's own country (nationality or residence) taxes; no Antarctic levy

sources.said: 2. No acts or activities taking place while the present Treaty is in force shall constitute a basis for asserting, supporting or denying a claim to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica or create any rights of sovereignty in Antarctica. … observers designated under paragraph 1 of Article VII and scientific personnel exchanged under subparagraph 1(b) of Article III of the Treaty, and members of the staffs accompanying any such persons, shall be subject only to the jurisdiction of the Contracting Party of which they are nationals in respect of all acts or omissions occurring while they are in Antarctica for the purpose of exercising their functions.
5. The Territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands. 6. The Australian Antarctic Territory.

The following persons are taxable – (a) persons in the employment of the British Antarctic Survey; and (b) other persons whose salaries and taxable allowances (or any part of such salaries or taxable allowances) in respect of their employment in the Territory are paid out of the funds of the British Antarctic Survey.
Taxable income is the income of a taxable person derived from that person’s employment in the Territory during a continuous period of at least 365 days.
the income tax which shall be levied on each taxable person shall be 7% of that person’s chargeable income.
Nothing in this section shall be construed as precluding the making of a provisional deduction from the salary of a taxable person

Le Traité de Washington n’exclut nullement l’application d’une fiscalité aux nationaux. La souveraineté de la France sur la Terre Adélie, dont la fiscalité est une illustration, est entière à l’égard des ressortissants français, même si elle n’est pas opposable aux ressortissants d’autres pays signataires.
